prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE production exploration asset: a 1536x1536 square atlas of SIX fixed side-view cave macro modules in an EXACT 2-column by 3-row grid. Every module is a 768x512 rectangular panel. Image 1 is the STRICT STRUCTURE GUIDE: preserve the six separate panel rectangles and preserve each panel's upper solid rock boundary and lower walkable floor boundary at its exact location. Paint the guide, do not redesign its silhouettes or move the floor. Image 2 is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: imitate its friendly hand-drawn thick dark outlines, enormous angular grey-brown rock masses, broad restrained flat shading, thick rock shoulders, sparse near-wall mineral flecks, small rubble and intimate dark grey backwalls. NO characters, no flashlight cones, no baked spotlight, no HUD or text. The atlas will be cut into six separate game modules and concatenated, so consistent illumination, scale and especially matching edges are crucial. Keep the outer 96 pixels of EVERY panel exactly as in the guide: straight level floor and ceiling, no protruding debris, no pillars blocking the opening, and consistent rock colors at all left/right edges. The neutral dark grey middle regions in Image 1 are OPEN AIR with a more distant quiet near-rock backwall; the muted brown above and below is opaque massive foreground stone. Preserve the thin warm floor highlight but make it discontinuous grey and tan bedrock, not a yellow highway. Render large polygonal rock faces in foreground, with cracks and modest facets; provide visibly thick supporting rock beneath the floor. Upper boundary may have small stalactites inside the guide's solid-rock envelope, but must never block the intended passage. Keep each full 768x512 tile filled to all four edges; zero outer margin, zero gutter, no framing, no grid lines or black panel separator lines. Floor should be very clear and continuous. Top-left panel: low uneven roof with a central shoulder and rolling stone floor. Top-right: gentle downward passage. Middle-left: gentle upward passage. Middle-right: expanded mineral chamber with a high arched roof and a few tiny amber inclusions embedded flush in near backwall. Bottom-left: irregular intimate mining alcove with expanded headroom and sparse chips near a wall. Bottom-right: low deep passage with overhanging rock shoulder. Use consistent subdued ambient lighting that is bright enough to inspect rock construction; do not make solid foreground black. Avoid a repeated wallpaper texture: each module must have unique carefully arranged large stone shapes and cracks, integrated into its own top and bottom masses. STRICT orthographic 2D side-view; no receding road, isometric perspective, photorealism, labels, watermark, artificial brickwork or interior vertical walls. Six DIFFERENT complete cave compositions on one atlas.
review: Actual output is 1254x1254. Six panels exist but requested silhouette and exact shared edges were not preserved. The generated original remains unchanged. Preview crops exclude divider pixels; art-profiles.json contains independently reviewed traces of the actual source. Rigid placement aligns floor endpoints, while fixed native rock cutouts cover part of each joint. This is a prototype technique and does not establish production-quality pixel-exact ports.
